text1: The result of early PTA developments in phase technology, though unable to travel as far as a normal phase skimmer, the larger body of the aggressive phase skimmer allows more charges to be stored.
text3: Teleports the ship an extremely short distance in the direction it's traveling. The system can store up to five charges at once.

text1: A vast network of nodes on this ships hull connects to the power core and shield generators. When activated this allows the ship to send electrical charges to eliminate incoming missiles, whilst keeping a damper field active to protect the ship.
text3: Briefly activates an energy field alongside lighting arcs which protects this ship from incoming fire and missiles.

text1: A continuation of phase research, the Shimmer core was designed from the ground up as a military project.  Intended to create a system with similar functionality to a phase cloak; the Scientists behind this project had a tall order to fill.  Though meeting few of the requirements, the project was successful enough to receive adoption into combat vessels.
text3: Provides a weak time distortion effect and dampens incoming fire.

text1:
Founded shortly after the declaration of the Hegemony, the Commonwealth of Zimowia-Ivernia is a union of the planetary governments of Zimowia and Ivernia. Often referred to simply as the Commonwealth; or occasionally as the Union of Iskala, after the capital of Zimowia in which the Commonwealth union was signed.  While the Commonwealth often keeps to itself, and notoriously has rigorous immigration controls, it is quite outspoken on several issues.  It has noticeably sided with the Persean League in claiming the Hegemony as illegitimate.  It also strictly outlaws Tri-Tachyon and the Luddic Church from operating in its controlled territory.  This has earned the ire of many within the Sector, but the strength and isolation of the Commonwealth has made it a secondary issue to most other polities.

Historical records of the Commonwealth are some of the most hotly debated records in the Persean Sector.  Denizens of the Commonwealth claim to hail from the Polaris Sector.  Should this be true then they would have traveled from some of the Domain core worlds across the Orion-Perseus abyss to reach the Persean Sector.  With the first recorded arrival of Commonwealth-associated ships a few decades after the collapse of the gate network, many dispute these claims.

A shining beacon of civility and habitability in the Persean Sector.  The locals insist that Zimowia is slightly colder than Old Earth, though no one can prove these claims.  Regardless this world is only matched by Gilead, a fact many luddics refuse to accept
text3: Zimowia winks at you on approach, massive cities twinkling in the distance flanked by rolling red forests, verdant wilderness, and Ice capped peaks which welcome your approach.  Zimowia was colonized and began terraformation decades before the end of the cold passage by remnants of a purported Polaris Treaty Alliance who arrived in the Persean sector.  Though Kotlinska presents itself as the representative of Lodowaziemia, numerous smaller polities retain control over their lands under the Kotlinski banner.  The collective efforts of these polities have resulted in a world matched only by Chicomoztoc in its scale of human endeavor.  Unlike many planets within the core worlds, Zimowia is fully self-sufficient on its own local goods.  Zimowia holds a unique sway within Fikenhild holo-entertainment, who constantly seek to have the Kotlinski king come for a visit to Fikenhild.  The natives of Zimowia are portrayed within Fikenhild holo-novels as honorable and traditional people

text1: A thin atmosphere clings to this world, allowing the massive dust plumes of the huge mobile refineries roving Agropelter�s surface to be clearly visible from space.  The lines of light made by these massive machines leading back to one of several massive industrial hubs.
text3: Upon approach, the sensor suite of your ship clicks softly; a quirk with Agropelter�s formation which led to a uniquely ionized magnetosphere.  All local infrastructure is heavily shielded, and the locals take safety with the utmost priority.  Its rich ore reserves and lack of any significantly achievable habitability lead the Kotlinksi to colonize Agropelter as its primary center of industry.  Massive industrial hubs lie beneath the Agropelter orbital shipyards, which produce the majority of all Commonwealth warships.  Agropelter is also host to the Commonwealth�s only large scale AM fuel production facilities.  Oft forgotten, Agropelters are portrayed by Fikenhild holo-entertainment as superstitious yet industrious.

text1: Despite the mild climate on Ivernia, the weapons-flare and electromagnetic noise of combat sputter through the commotion of Ivernia�s giant urban centers and cloud coverage.  Patrolling warships can be seen conducting localized AM purges of the planet's surface.
text3: Originally terraformed into a terran eccentric world, then colonized by a large contingent of Domain settler; [the CEO] was quick to take over the planet a few decades before the end of the cold passage.  His brutal conquest forced the majority of the planet's settlers into the wilderness of the planet.  During [the CEO] crazed last few years, he engineered a series of man-hunting wildlife and released them into the Ivernian wilderness.  Building large walled urban centers from which ‘civilized’ society under the thumb of [The CEO] would operate.  These man-hunters could of course reproduce, and have been extraordinarily difficult to eradicate from the planet's biosphere.  The planet's terraformation from eccentric to a full terran world required severely bio-engineered organisms to compete with the man-hunters, meaning all cities have to be walled off and protected from the native fauna.  Farming as a result is nigh-impossible without a complex network of autonomous drones and soil nanites, as the local wildlife are quick to consume nutrients from any unprotected source.  Obviously most remaining domain settlers refuse to parlay with the Iverinan government, despite numerous attempts.  Regular airdrops of supplies are launched into 'decivilized' regions by patrolling warships as a gesture of goodwill.

text1: This world should not exist.  The last Domain records show this world as a cryovolcanic world far too cold to have a water surface.  Yet here Vanduo stands, with its thick atmosphere obscuring any peek behind the curtain to what waits below.
text3: Containing all resources required to fuel further colonization, the world which would become known as Atrimpas was colonized as quickly as possible by the Domain.  With the arrival of the Polarian Expedition, the world was taken over by (the CEO) alongside Ivernia to act as a base of operations. Shortly after (the CEO) was killed, it became a part of Ivernia.  The thick atmosphere is mostly breathable, though high concentrations of sulfur compounds and carbon monoxide prevent true breathability.  In spite of this, large hostile sealife prowls the ocean floor alongside the autonomous bores which scrape minerals from the seabed and mantle.  Going completely unrecorded in all Domain records, the local sealife poses a constant threat to the platforms hosting the majority of Atrimpas’s population. Miners retrieving ores from the autonomous bores are an especially superstitious bunch, as their water craft are easy prey to the leviathans which prowl the deep.  Heavy weapons are a popular trade commodity here, as the defense systems are constantly getting damaged by the denizens of the seas.
